tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Existence of Local Defining Functions] 1. chA:A.27Suppose $\tilde{M}$ is a smooth manifold and $M \subseteq \tilde{M}$ is an embedded submanifold of codimension $k$. For each point $p \in M$, there exist a neighborhood $U$ of $p$ in $\tilde{M}$ and a smooth submersion $\Phi : U \to \mathbb {R}^k$ such that $M \cap U$ is a level set of $\Phi $.

If $M \subseteq \tilde{M}$ is a submanifold (immersed or embedded), the inclusion map $\iota : M \hookrightarrow \tilde{M}$ induces an injective linear map $d\iota _p : T_p M \to T_p \tilde{M}$ for each $p \in M$. It is standard practice to identify $T_p M$ with its image $d\iota _p(T_p M) \subseteq T_p \tilde{M}$, thus regarding $T_p M$ as a subspace of $T_p \tilde{M}$. The next proposition gives two handy ways to identify this subspace in the embedded case.
